draft.title: Spread of cultural trends
card: A cultural trend is a style of music, fashion or entertainment that many people take up for a time. Trends used to spread slowly, through radio, cinema, magazines and the movement of people.
Streaming services and social media now let songs, clips and styles reach people in many countries within hours or days. Anyone with a phone and an internet connection can share or watch them.
Because of this, a trend can start anywhere, such as a bedroom in Seoul or a small town in Nigeria. It does not have to begin in a big media centre like Los Angeles.
A trend that spreads widely can reach people far from where it began. Some places then share similar music, clothes and shows, though people may also adapt a trend to suit their own culture.
draft.remember: Streaming and social media let trends start anywhere and reach many places fast.

a.q: Why do music and fashion trends now spread around the world faster than they once did?
opts: Streaming and social media share them instantly online
Radio and cinema now reach more countries than before
Governments agree which trends each country will adopt
Large media centres produce all trends and then export them
a.why: Streaming and social media let people share songs and styles within hours, wherever they live. Radio and cinema were the older, slower ways, and trends can now start outside big media centres.
a.clue: Think about what a phone and an internet connection let people do.

b.q: Tane, a teenager in Rotorua, posts a dance clip online. Within a week, students in Brazil and Japan are copying it. What does this show about cultural trends?
opts: A trend can start anywhere and reach many places
A trend must start in a large media centre first
A trend spreads only through radio and magazines
A trend stays within the country where it began
b.why: The dance began with one teenager in a small city and reached other continents within days. This shows trends can start anywhere. The wrong options describe older, slower ways of spreading or say a big centre is needed, which the example does not support.
b.clue: Where did the clip start, and who ended up copying it?

a.best: Streaming and social media share them instantly online

b.best: A trend can start anywhere and reach many places

b.q: Tane, a teenager in Rotorua, posts a dance clip online. Within a week, students in Brazil and Japan are copying it. What does this show about cultural trends?

Online trends spread most within the country they start in
